children: Metal must survive $70 resistance and a rather uncomfortable Fed speech.
Silver returns to $70
Silver
pumped above $70 an ounce Friday for the first time since mid-June, reaching a ten-week high.
The metal is heading for its fourth consecutive weekly advance, extending a recovery that has lifted prices from roughly $55–$56 around the final week of July.
The $70 threshold carries both technical and psychological significance. Round numbers often attract profit-taking, pending sell orders and breakout traders simultaneously.
A convincing close above it could strengthen momentum; another sharp rejection would suggest buyers are not quite ready to reclaim higher ground.

Silver has outperformed gold during the latest leg of the precious-metals rally. Gold retreated under $4,600 Friday, while silver’s stronger weekly performance compressed the gold–silver ratio — the number of silver ounces required to buy one ounce of gold — to roughly 65.
Two demand stories meet

Like gold, silver has benefited from concerns about US debt, expanded Treasury bond buybacks and long-term dollar purchasing power. That “debasement trade” encourages investors to buy scarce assets when policy intervention appears likely to weaken conventional currencies.

Silver is also an industrial material used in electronics, solar panels, electric vehicles and data centers. That gives it two demand engines: investors seeking monetary protection and manufacturers requiring physical metal.
The global silver market is expected to remain in structural deficit for a sixth consecutive year, meaning demand exceeds newly available supply.
Mine production has struggled to respond because much of the world’s silver is produced as a by-product of mining other metals, limiting how quickly output can increase.

July core inflation accelerated to 3.7%, leaving markets pricing around a 35% probability of a September rate increase. Higher rates support the dollar and raise the opportunity cost of holding metals, which produce no income.
A sustained move above $70 could expose the $72 area, followed by the Q2-2026 trading zone around $75. Initial support sits near $68, then $65.
Silver’s larger price swings make confirmation especially important; a brief intraday visit above resistance does not automatically become a permanent address.
